translation_en: ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad narrated to me: ‘Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma‘mar informed us. He said: Al-Zuhri informed me. He said: ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me, from al-Miswar ibn Makhramah and Marwan, each of whom confirmed the other’s account. He said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, set out at the time of al-Hudaybiyyah. When they were partway along the road, the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘Khalid ibn al-Walid is at al-Ghamim with a cavalry detachment of Quraysh, acting as their advance guard, so take the road to the right.’ By Allah, Khalid did not notice them until the army’s dust was before him. He set off at a gallop to warn Quraysh. The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, continued until he reached the mountain pass from which they would descend to them. There his riding camel knelt down. The people said, ‘Get up! Get up!’ but it persisted. They said, ‘Al-Qaswa’ has become stubborn! Al-Qaswa’ has become stubborn!’ The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘Al-Qaswa’ has not become stubborn, and that is not her nature. Rather, the One who restrained the elephant has restrained her.’ Then he said, ‘By the One in Whose hand is my soul, they will not ask me for any proposal that honors the sacred limits of Allah without my granting it to them.’ He urged her on, and she sprang up. He turned away from them and camped at the far end of al-Hudaybiyyah, beside a small pool with little water, from which the people were drawing it a little at a time. The people soon used up its water. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, was told that they were thirsty. He drew an arrow from his quiver and told them to put it into the pool. By Allah, water kept welling up for them until they left it. While they were there, Budayl ibn Warqa’ al-Khuza‘i arrived with a group of his people from Khuza‘ah. They were trusted advisers of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, from the people of Tihamah. He said, ‘I left Ka‘b ibn Lu’ayy and ‘Amir ibn Lu’ayy camped at the water sources of al-Hudaybiyyah. With them are the suckling camels and their young. They will fight you and keep you from the House.’ The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘We have not come to fight anyone. We have come to perform ‘umrah. War has worn Quraysh out and harmed them. If they wish, I will make a truce with them for a set time, and they will leave me free to meet the people. If I prevail, they may join what the people have joined, if they wish; otherwise, they will have time to recover. If they refuse, then by the One in Whose hand is my soul, I will fight them for this cause until my neck is cut off, and Allah will certainly bring His command to pass.’ Budayl said, ‘I will convey what you say to them.’ He went to Quraysh and said, ‘We have come to you from this man and heard him say something. If you want us to present it to you, we will.’ The foolish among them said, ‘We have no need for you to tell us anything about him.’ But those among them with sound judgment said, ‘Tell us what you heard him say.’ He said, ‘I heard him say such-and-such,’ and told them what the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, had said. ‘Urwah ibn Mas‘ud stood up and said, ‘My people, am I not like a father to you?’ They said, ‘Yes.’ He said, ‘And am I not like a son to you?’ They said, ‘Yes.’ He said, ‘Do you suspect me?’ They said, ‘No.’ He said, ‘Do you not know that I called the people of ‘Ukaz to join you, but when they held back from me, I came to you with my family, my children, and those who obeyed me?’ They said, ‘Yes.’ He said, ‘This man has offered you a sound proposal. Accept it, and let me go to him.’ They said, ‘Go to him.’ He went to him and began speaking with the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. The Prophet said to him much the same as he had said to Budayl. ‘Urwah then said, ‘Muhammad, tell me: if you wipe out your own people, have you ever heard of an Arab who wiped out his people before you? But if the other outcome happens, by Allah, I see faces and a motley group of people who are likely to flee and leave you.’ Abu Bakr said to him, ‘Suck the clitoris of al-Lat! Are we to flee from him and abandon him?’ He asked, ‘Who is that?’ They said, ‘Abu Bakr.’ He said, ‘By the One in Whose hand is my soul, were it not for a favor you once did for me, which I have not repaid, I would answer you.’ As ‘Urwah spoke with the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, he repeatedly reached for his beard. Al-Mughirah ibn Shu‘bah was standing at the Prophet’s head with a sword and wearing a helmet. Whenever ‘Urwah reached his hand toward the Prophet’s beard, al-Mughirah struck his hand with the flat of the sword and said, ‘Keep your hand away from the beard of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him.’ ‘Urwah raised his head and asked, ‘Who is this?’ They said, ‘Al-Mughirah ibn Shu‘bah.’ He said, ‘You treacherous one! Am I not still trying to make amends for your treachery?’ In pre-Islamic times, al-Mughirah had accompanied a group of people, killed them, and taken their property. He then came and accepted Islam. The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘As for Islam, I accept it; as for the property, I have nothing to do with it.’ ‘Urwah began watching the Prophet’s companions closely. By Allah, whenever the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, spat, it fell into the hand of one of them, who rubbed it over his face and skin. Whenever he gave them an order, they hastened to carry it out. When he performed ablution, they nearly fought over the water he had used. When he spoke, they lowered their voices in his presence, and out of respect for him they did not stare at him. ‘Urwah returned to his companions and said, ‘My people, by Allah, I have been sent as an envoy to kings. I have been to Caesar, Khosrow, and the Negus. By Allah, I have never seen a king whose companions honored him as much as Muhammad’s companions honor Muhammad, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. By Allah, whenever he spat, it fell into the hand of one of them, who rubbed it over his face and skin. Whenever he gave them an order, they hastened to carry it out. When he performed ablution, they nearly fought over the water he had used. When he spoke, they lowered their voices in his presence, and out of respect for him they did not stare at him. He has offered you a sound proposal, so accept it.’ A man from Banu Kinanah said, ‘Let me go to him.’ They said, ‘Go to him.’ When he came into view of the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and his companions, the Messenger of Allah said, ‘This is so-and-so. He comes from a people who honor sacrificial camels, so send them out to him.’ They sent the camels out, and the people greeted him with the pilgrims’ chant. When he saw that, he said, ‘Glory be to Allah! These people should not be kept from the House.’ When he returned to his companions, he said, ‘I saw that the sacrificial camels had been garlanded and marked. I do not think they should be kept from the House.’ A man among them called Mikraz ibn Hafs stood up and said, ‘Let me go to him.’ They said, ‘Go to him.’ When he came into view of them, the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘This is Mikraz, a wicked man.’ He began speaking with the Prophet. While he was speaking with him, Suhayl ibn ‘Amr arrived. Ma‘mar said: Ayyub informed me, from ‘Ikrimah, that when Suhayl ibn ‘Amr arrived, the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘Your matter has become easier for you.’ Ma‘mar said: Al-Zuhri said in his report: Suhayl ibn ‘Amr came and said, ‘Come, let us write a document between us and you.’ The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, called for the scribe. The Prophet said, ‘In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.’ Suhayl said, ‘As for the Most Compassionate, by Allah, I do not know what that is. Write instead, “In Your name, O Allah,” as you used to write.’ The Muslims said, ‘By Allah, we will write only, “In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.”’ The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘Write, “In Your name, O Allah.”’ Then he said, ‘This is what Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, has agreed to.’ Suhayl said, ‘By Allah, if we knew that you were the Messenger of Allah, we would not have kept you from the House or fought you. Write “Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah” instead.’ The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘By Allah, I am the Messenger of Allah, even if you deny me. Write “Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah.”’ Al-Zuhri said: This was because of his words, ‘They will not ask me for any proposal that honors the sacred limits of Allah without my granting it to them.’ The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, then said to Suhayl, ‘On the condition that you let us reach the House and circumambulate it.’ Suhayl said, ‘By Allah, the Arabs will not say that we were overcome by force. Rather, that will be next year.’ So it was written. Suhayl then said, ‘And on the condition that any man who comes to you from us, even if he follows your religion, you will return him to us.’ The Muslims said, ‘Glory be to Allah! How can someone who has come as a Muslim be returned to the polytheists?’ While they were speaking, Abu Jandal ibn Suhayl ibn ‘Amr came in, dragging his chains. He had escaped from the lower part of Makkah and thrown himself among the Muslims. Suhayl said, ‘This, Muhammad, is the first person I am making a settlement with you about: you must return him to me.’ The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘We have not yet finished the document.’ He said, ‘Then by Allah, I will never make peace with you over anything.’ The Prophet said, ‘Let him go to me.’ He said, ‘I will not let him go to you.’ The Prophet said, ‘Do it, then.’ He said, ‘I will not do it.’ Mikraz said, ‘We have agreed to let him go to you.’ Abu Jandal said, ‘Muslims, am I to be returned to the polytheists when I have come to you as a Muslim? Do you not see what I have suffered?’ He had been tortured severely for Allah’s sake. ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab said: I went to the Prophet of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and said, ‘Are you truly the Prophet of Allah?’ He said, ‘Yes.’ I said, ‘Are we not upon the truth and our enemy upon falsehood?’ He said, ‘Yes.’ I said, ‘Then why should we accept a humiliating concession in our religion?’ He said, ‘I am the Messenger of Allah, and I do not disobey Him. He is my supporter.’ I said, ‘Did you not used to tell us that we would come to the House and circumambulate it?’ He said, ‘Yes. But did I tell you that we would come to it this year?’ I said, ‘No.’ He said, ‘Then you will come to it and circumambulate it.’’ ‘Umar said: I then went to Abu Bakr and said, ‘Abu Bakr, is he not truly the Prophet of Allah?’ He said, ‘Yes.’ I said, ‘Are we not upon the truth and our enemy upon falsehood?’ He said, ‘Yes.’ I said, ‘Then why should we accept a humiliating concession in our religion?’ He said, ‘Man, he is the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. He does not disobey his Lord, and He is his supporter. Hold firmly to his course, for by Allah he is upon the truth.’ I said, ‘Did he not used to tell us that we would come to the House and circumambulate it?’ He said, ‘Yes. But did he tell you that you would come to it this year?’ I said, ‘No.’ He said, ‘Then you will come to it and circumambulate it.’’ Al-Zuhri said: ‘Umar said, ‘I did good deeds because of that.’ When the writing of the agreement was finished, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said to his companions, ‘Get up, slaughter your sacrificial camels, then shave your heads.’ By Allah, not one man among them got up, even after he had repeated that three times. When no one got up, he went to Umm Salamah and told her what he had encountered from the people. Umm Salamah said, ‘Prophet of Allah, do you want them to do it? Go out, and do not say a word to any of them until you have slaughtered your sacrificial camels and called your barber to shave your head.’ He went out and did not speak to any of them until he had done that: he slaughtered his sacrificial camels and called his barber, who shaved his head. When they saw that, they got up and slaughtered their camels, and they began shaving one another, until some of them nearly killed one another from grief. Then believing women came to him, and Allah Most High revealed, ‘Believers, when believing women come to you as emigrants, examine them’ until the words ‘the marital bonds of disbelieving women’ (60:10). That day ‘Umar divorced two wives he had while they remained in polytheism. Mu‘awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan married one of them, and Safwan ibn Umayyah married the other. Then the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, returned to Madinah. Abu Basir, a man from Quraysh who was a Muslim, came to him. They sent two men to pursue him and said, ‘Honor the agreement you made with us.’ So he handed Abu Basir over to the two men. They set out with him until they reached Dhu al-Hulayfah, where they stopped to eat some dates they had with them. Abu Basir said to one of the men, ‘By Allah, so-and-so, I think your sword is a fine one.’ The other man drew it and said, ‘Yes, by Allah, it is fine. I have tested it, then tested it again.’ Abu Basir said, ‘Let me see it.’ The man handed it to him, and Abu Basir struck him with it until he was dead. The other man fled until he reached Madinah. He ran into the mosque. When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, saw him, he said, ‘This man has seen something terrifying.’ When he reached the Prophet, he said, ‘By Allah, my companion has been killed, and I will be killed too.’ Abu Basir then came and said, ‘Prophet of Allah, by Allah, Allah has fulfilled your pledge. You returned me to them, then Allah rescued me from them.’ The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘His mother’s woe! He would kindle a war if he had anyone.’ When Abu Basir heard that, he realized that the Prophet would send him back to them, so he went out until he reached the coast. Abu Jandal ibn Suhayl escaped from them and joined Abu Basir. Every man from Quraysh who became a Muslim and escaped would join Abu Basir, until a group had gathered around him. By Allah, whenever they heard of a caravan belonging to Quraysh setting out for Syria, they intercepted it, killed its men, and took their property. Quraysh then appealed to the Prophet, by Allah and by their kinship, to send for them, promising that whoever came to him would be safe. The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, sent for them. Then Allah Most High revealed, ‘He is the One who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Makkah, after He had given you victory over them’ until the words ‘the zeal of the time of ignorance’ (48:24; 48:1). Their zeal was that they did not acknowledge that he was the Prophet of Allah, did not acknowledge ‘In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful,’ and prevented them from reaching the House.
